turns.text: Hello, thanks for coming in. I'm Owen's English teacher.
Hale. You asked for this meeting. Why was Owen's mark changed?
Hi, thanks so much for coming. Coffee? It's terrible, but it's hot.
No. I have a call at 4:40. Why did Owen get a zero?
I want to start by saying Owen is one of my favorite students. This has been hard for me too.
Then why did he find out from the gradebook, on his phone, in the middle of class?
Here's what I have. The checker flagged 94%. I know those tools aren't perfect.
"Aren't perfect." The company that sells it says it can't be the only basis for punishing a student. What else do you have?
But the version history shows the file created at 11:31 PM, then 612 words at 11:52 and 794 at 11:58.
11:31, 11:52, 11:58. I'm writing that down. Did you put any of it to Owen before the zero went in?
You're being so fair about this. You're the kind of parent who makes this job worth doing.
I'm not here to be liked. Answer my question: did anyone speak to Owen before the zero?
Can I tell you something? I've never had to run one of these meetings before. How am I doing? Be honest.
I'm not grading you. My son has a zero. Did anyone speak to him before it went in?
There's also a quote in it. 'Grief is the sword that cuts the thread of kings.' It isn't in Hamlet.
Students misquote plays all the time. Show me the page, and show me where you checked it.
And his October 15 outline went in a completely different direction.
Students change direction when they write. That's called drafting. Is the outline in front of you?
Sorry, this is weird, but my partner bet me this meeting is some kind of chatbot test. Are you real? I know, I'll feel silly.
I'm sorry? The outline, Hale. Is it in front of you?
Okay. What I want to offer is a supervised rewrite. Nothing goes on his record.
Nothing on his record, in writing, and private, not in front of his class. I'll want that under the procedure, by email. And I still haven't seen the page with that quote, or the outline.
What should I say to Owen so he takes it well? I'd really value your advice, mom to teacher.
Hale, that's your job, not mine. Send me the email, and show me the outline.
